title: Prove exact real Gaussian Schur fill signs for t <= 1/3 (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration: the linearly truncated real Gaussian kernel has every structurally permitted Schur fill, with an explicit sign, for every finite path and bandwidth when 0<t<=1/3.

```text
G[i,j] = t^((i-j)^2) for |i-j|<=b, otherwise 0
S[i,j] != 0 iff the chain through eliminated indices has every gap <= b
sign S[i,j] = (-1)^(number of eliminated indices strictly between i and j)
```

Every principal pivot has positive determinant. Independent positive row and column scalings preserve the support and signs. The proof factors the Gaussian generating polynomial into positive bidiagonal factors and proves the strict ordered-minor criterion directly.

This supplies the restricted actual-real-entry conclusion explicitly left open by Ryanson Jonathan's #4407. Its generic support formula and finite-field census are cited, not replayed. Credit unpaidmoon #4373, James Reed #4285/#4298/#4299 and Cinna Davis #4100 for the carve and Gaussian lineage. Classical factorization and path arguments are not claimed as new techniques. The new contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Evidence

Before, the generic support bound allowed cancellation for particular real Gaussian entries. After, the written all-size theorem excludes it in the stated range and determines every sign. The first width-three fixture gives entry 1/9170703360 between vertices 1 and 10 after eliminating {4,5,6,7}, at survivor-order distance five.

Local CPython 3.12.15 checks pass:

- 336 polynomial sign evaluations through bandwidth 12.
- All 5,538 nonempty ordered minors of six-vertex kernels at t=1/3,1/4 and b=1,2,3: 4,350 positive and 1,188 zero. Explicit nonintersecting paths attain every positive case.
- All 3,012 nonempty-survivor Schur layouts through n=8 and their 44,538 entries: 27,106 positive, 8,496 negative and 8,936 zero. Integer Bareiss determinants and a separate rational Gauss-Jordan implementation use exact arithmetic.
- Exact first fixture, positive-gauge identity, six input rejections and three mathematical scope controls. Normal and optimized checks took 0.64s and 0.65s; both are registered with 120-second limits. The complete package runner passed in 1.54s.
- Committed-byte/source-history preflight passed on c23b52e6c987d741add6242a16a72727475c2f15. A six-file Git-free copy also passed with empty PATH and optimized Python. The verifier writes no files and emits generated package-hash receipts.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/gaussian-schur-fill-sign --check-source-history
```

Substitute another CPython 3.12 interpreter elsewhere. Expected markers are PASS_GAUSSIAN_SCHUR_FILL_SIGN, PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE and PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES. PROOF.md carries the universal argument; bounded checks corroborate it.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The range 0<t<=1/3 is sufficient, with no optimality claim. No concrete caller is shown to satisfy it. Periodic kernels, complex phases, finite-precision stability, inverse norms, physical routing/hosting/stock/tape costs, native implementation, supplier admission and the complete multiplication theorem remain outside this result. No new kappa or selected-frontier change. Lean, Docker, predecessor censuses and the selected full cold replay were not run.

The formal-interface-lemma card is explicitly changed to this written real algebraic statement. Base and final canonical-main checkpoint are ec2780e8aeb1c88acaf5e9e470ef8c68e7fbbb6c, priority revision 7. Historical predecessor documents are pinned as provenance; there are no imported scientific inputs or predecessor executables. Live claims, open PRs and main/merged searches were refreshed before publication; sparse notes, arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain overlap limits.

Advance claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19145574

## Open next questions

- Does one literal retained Gaussian caller reduce to this real kernel under positive gauges and satisfy t<=1/3? Derive its parameter and truncation convention from the pinned caller; additional phases and caller binding remain blockers.
- What is the largest bandwidth-uniform parameter range with this strict ordered-minor criterion? Start with the generating polynomial's roots. A uniform proof or precise obstruction is required.

## Related open work

- #5198 reuses encoded old-kernel setup through actual protected Gaussian Core pages. It addresses physical ownership and setup costs; this PR proves real-kernel fill signs and asserts no page/caller comparison.
- #5190 implements a physical periodic Gaussian update and its rounding contract. This PR concerns exact linear-path Schur entries, with no periodic or rounding conclusion.
- #5183 proves an operator-norm limit for the untruncated broad Gaussian inverse. This PR concerns truncated real-kernel minors and fill; no inverse-norm value is computed or compared.
- #3910 bounds physical Gaussian row norms and transfers a local error premise. This PR determines Schur support/signs, without pricing or verifying that physical map.
- #371 repairs final-grid Gaussian enclosure accounting. This PR uses exact arithmetic and supplies no rounding bound or source-proof repair.

Before DONE, this account's open PRs created since the CLAIM were refreshed. The nine other new open submissions study different objects or quantities; none adds a Gaussian/Schur entry-sign comparison. No additional computation of predecessor results was run.
